title: HPSC Food Safety Officer — Unit 3 Part A: Food Chemistry (Macromolecules) — 100 MCQs

source_scope.primary_basis: Uploaded Unit 3 Part A master study handout, 97 pages.

modules.coverage: Water molecular structure and properties; water holding and bound water; ion–dipole, hydrophilic and hydrophobic interactions; water activity and ERH; sorption isotherms, zones, glass transition and hysteresis; water-activity effects on stability; moisture determination by thermal drying, distillation and Karl Fischer titration.

Monosaccharide and oligosaccharide classification; homopolysaccharides and heteropolysaccharides; amylose and amylopectin; gelatinization, gelation, retrogradation and staling; modified starches; pectin and degree of esterification; agar, alginate, carrageenan, guar and locust bean gums; cellulose, glycogen, hemicellulose, dextrins and enzyme specificity.

Isoelectric point, amphoteric behaviour, salting-in/out and protein classes; denaturation and processing reactions; deamidation, racemization and oxidation; alkaline β-elimination and cross-links; plant-protein fibre spinning and extrusion; gluten, casein/chymosin and egg-white proteins.

Maillard initiation, Amadori products, reaction conditions, Strecker degradation, melanoidins, lysine loss and acrylamide precursor; caramelization; PPO/copper enzyme chemistry, cresolase and catecholase activity, quinones and industrial control by blanching, acidification, ascorbic acid, oxygen restriction, sulfites and chelation.

source_scope.source_integrity: The question bank follows the accessible content and qualifications in the uploaded handout. Where the handout itself marks a detail as verification-required or flags an internal source error, the bank avoids treating that detail as an unqualified source-verified fact.

exam_alignment.current_pattern_summary: Public reports on HPSC Advertisement No. 25/2026 describe a Screening Test (if held) focused on General Studies and Haryana GK, followed by a 150-mark, 3-hour subjective Subject Knowledge Test. The Subject Knowledge Test is reported to carry 87.5% of final merit and the interview 12.5%. Verify the final scheme and any corrigenda directly on the HPSC website.
exam_alignment.important_distinction: This is a 100-question objective practice bank for active recall and technical revision. It is NOT a literal reproduction of the reported 2026 Subject Knowledge Test format, which is subjective/descriptive. The technical content in this handout is more directly relevant to the Subject Knowledge syllabus than to a General Studies/Haryana-GK screening paper.
exam_alignment.style_adaptation: Questions emphasize precise definitions, molecular mechanisms, process sequences, numerical interpretation, correct/incorrect statement pairs, source-specific qualifiers, industrial application and common examiner traps. Twenty questions use the count-based three-statement format found in the uploaded handout's Stage 1 revision banks.
exam_alignment.prediction_caveat: No reliable method can calculate the probability that a particular generated question will appear in the examination. The bank prioritizes syllabus relevance and examinable concepts, not guaranteed predictions.
exam_alignment.historical_context: Earlier HPSC FSO papers may be useful for historical question-style practice, but the current recruitment scheme should take precedence over older paper formats.

question_design.question_order: All questions and options appear before the answer key.
question_design.answer_key_order: The consolidated answer key appears after all 100 questions.
question_design.explanation_order: All detailed explanations appear after the complete answer key.
question_design.coverage_strategy: Balanced coverage across the four modules, with additional emphasis on high-yield distinctions, process mechanisms, numerical relationships, source corrections and application-based interpretation.

scoring_note: No official marking scheme is assigned to this practice file. Apply the marking scheme in the current HPSC notification when conducting a timed mock.

detailed_explanations.detailed_explanation: The handout gives approximately 104.5° for the vapour-state H–O–H angle. Do not confuse it with the ideal tetrahedral angle of 109.5°.
detailed_explanations.source_reference: Directly supported by the uploaded Unit 3 Part A handout.

detailed_explanations.correct_answer: Unequal sharing of O–H bonding electrons creates partial charges
detailed_explanations.detailed_explanation: Oxygen attracts shared electrons more strongly, producing partial negative charge on oxygen and partial positive charges on hydrogen. The molecule remains neutral overall; the O–H bond is polar covalent, not completely ionic.
detailed_explanations.source_reference: Directly supported by the uploaded Unit 3 Part A handout.

detailed_explanations.correct_answer: Donate two and accept two hydrogen bonds
detailed_explanations.detailed_explanation: The model describes two hydrogen-bond donor directions through hydrogen atoms and two acceptor directions through oxygen lone-pair directions. In liquid water these associations are dynamic, not permanent.
detailed_explanations.source_reference: Directly supported by the uploaded Unit 3 Part A handout.

detailed_explanations.detailed_explanation: Vaporization requires molecules to escape the cohesive liquid network, so substantial energy is needed. This is why drying water-rich foods has a significant energy demand.
detailed_explanations.source_reference: Directly supported by the uploaded Unit 3 Part A handout.

detailed_explanations.detailed_explanation: Near 4°C, disruption of the relatively open hydrogen-bonded arrangement initially permits more compact packing. Above this temperature, thermal expansion predominates and density falls.
detailed_explanations.source_reference: Directly supported by the uploaded Unit 3 Part A handout.

detailed_explanations.detailed_explanation: The first statement is correct: liquid water has a dynamic hydrogen-bond network. The second turns an idealized bonding capacity into permanent occupancy, which is incorrect. The third confuses liquid water with an ordered ice-like lattice. Thus, exactly one statement is correct.
detailed_explanations.source_reference: Directly supported by the uploaded Unit 3 Part A handout.

detailed_explanations.correct_answer: The ability of a food matrix to retain liquid water against flow
detailed_explanations.detailed_explanation: Water holding capacity is a matrix-level retention property. A gel may prevent bulk liquid flow while individual water molecules still move and participate in reactions.
detailed_explanations.source_reference: Directly supported by the uploaded Unit 3 Part A handout.

detailed_explanations.correct_answer: Separation or expulsion of liquid from the gel network
detailed_explanations.detailed_explanation: Syneresis is liquid separation from a gel. It indicates loss or rearrangement of matrix retention, not necessarily removal of all molecularly associated water.
detailed_explanations.source_reference: Directly supported by the uploaded Unit 3 Part A handout.

detailed_explanations.correct_answer: Oxygen ends toward the positive ion
detailed_explanations.detailed_explanation: The oxygen end carries a partial negative charge and is attracted to a positive sodium ion. Around a negative chloride ion, the hydrogen-rich positive ends orient toward the ion.
detailed_explanations.source_reference: Directly supported by the uploaded Unit 3 Part A handout.

detailed_explanations.detailed_explanation: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Association of apolar regions reduces the interface with water and contributes to protein folding. It is not a new covalent bond, so statement 2 is false. Count = 2.
detailed_explanations.source_reference: Directly supported by the uploaded Unit 3 Part A handout.

detailed_explanations.detailed_explanation: At equilibrium, aw ≈ ERH/100. Thus 72% ERH corresponds to aw ≈ 0.72. This does not mean the food contains 72% moisture.
detailed_explanations.source_reference: Directly supported by the uploaded Unit 3 Part A handout.

detailed_explanations.detailed_explanation: The handout gives aw = f/f0 ≈ p/p0 = ERH/100, with the food and pure-water reference evaluated at the same temperature.
detailed_explanations.source_reference: Directly supported by the uploaded Unit 3 Part A handout.

detailed_explanations.detailed_explanation: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Water activity is not identical to moisture content; foods with different matrices can have different aw at the same moisture percentage. The vapour-pressure ratio compares food and pure water at the same temperature.
detailed_explanations.source_reference: Directly supported by the uploaded Unit 3 Part A handout.

detailed_explanations.correct_answer: Equilibrium moisture content to water activity at constant temperature
detailed_explanations.detailed_explanation: A sorption isotherm describes equilibrium moisture content against water activity at a fixed temperature. It is used in dehydration, packaging and stability decisions.
detailed_explanations.source_reference: Directly supported by the uploaded Unit 3 Part A handout.

detailed_explanations.correct_answer: Sugars and other small soluble molecules
detailed_explanations.detailed_explanation: The handout associates a J-shaped Type III curve with sugar-rich and other small-solute-rich foods. Many foods show a sigmoidal Type II curve.
detailed_explanations.source_reference: Directly supported by the uploaded Unit 3 Part A handout.

detailed_explanations.detailed_explanation: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Hysteresis is the non-superimposition of adsorption/resorption and desorption curves and depends partly on sample history. An isotherm relates equilibrium moisture content to water activity at constant temperature, not time.
detailed_explanations.source_reference: Directly supported by the uploaded Unit 3 Part A handout.

detailed_explanations.detailed_explanation: Zone III is the bulk aqueous fraction, with the highest mobility and solvent availability. Zone I is most strongly associated; Zone II has substantial plasticizing effects.
detailed_explanations.source_reference: Directly supported by the uploaded Unit 3 Part A handout.

detailed_explanations.detailed_explanation: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. The Maillard optimum is a qualified schematic near 0.6–0.7. Lipid oxidation is non-monotonic in the source schematic, with an initial decline and later rise. Lowering aw can inhibit growth but does not automatically kill microorganisms or remove preformed hazards.
detailed_explanations.source_reference: Directly supported by the uploaded Unit 3 Part A handout.

detailed_explanations.detailed_explanation: The source schematic places a maximum near aw 0.6–0.7: very low aw restricts mobility, while high aw can dilute reactants. This is a qualified teaching relationship, not a universal constant.
detailed_explanations.source_reference: Directly supported by the uploaded Unit 3 Part A handout.

detailed_explanations.detailed_explanation: Initial sample mass = 35−30 = 5 g; apparent water loss = 35−34 = 1 g. Wet-basis moisture = 1/5 × 100 = 20%. Dry-basis moisture would be 1/4 × 100 = 25%.
detailed_explanations.source_reference: Directly supported by the uploaded Unit 3 Part A handout.

detailed_explanations.detailed_explanation: Fructose is a six-carbon ketose, whereas glucose and galactose are aldoses. Ribose is a five-carbon aldose.
detailed_explanations.source_reference: Directly supported by the uploaded Unit 3 Part A handout.

detailed_explanations.detailed_explanation: Homopolysaccharides contain one principal monomer type. Branching does not make a polymer heterogeneous; amylopectin is branched but glucose-based.
detailed_explanations.source_reference: Directly supported by the uploaded Unit 3 Part A handout.

detailed_explanations.detailed_explanation: Inulin is fructose-based and is correctly identified as a fructan. Amylose, cellulose and glycogen are glucose-based homopolysaccharides.
detailed_explanations.source_reference: Directly supported by the uploaded Unit 3 Part A handout.

detailed_explanations.detailed_explanation: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Amylose is mainly linear α(1→4)-linked glucose; amylopectin has α(1→4) chains and α(1→6) branches. Branching does not create a second monomer type, so amylopectin remains a glucose homopolysaccharide.
detailed_explanations.source_reference: Directly supported by the uploaded Unit 3 Part A handout.

detailed_explanations.detailed_explanation: Lactose and maltose have reducing ends. Sucrose is non-reducing because both anomeric centres participate in its glycosidic linkage.
detailed_explanations.source_reference: Directly supported by the uploaded Unit 3 Part A handout.

detailed_explanations.detailed_explanation: Amylose is predominantly linear with α(1→4) glycosidic linkages. Amylopectin also has α(1→4) chains but includes α(1→6) branch points.
detailed_explanations.source_reference: Directly supported by the uploaded Unit 3 Part A handout.

detailed_explanations.detailed_explanation: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The handout reports blue iodine colour for amylose and describes amylopectin as highly branched. Amylose reassociates more rapidly; amylopectin contributes to slower storage-related reorganization.
detailed_explanations.source_reference: Directly supported by the uploaded Unit 3 Part A handout.

detailed_explanations.correct_answer: Amylose reassociates more rapidly than amylopectin
detailed_explanations.detailed_explanation: The handout describes amylose as predominantly linear and more rapidly reassociating, while amylopectin is highly branched and reorganizes more slowly during storage.
detailed_explanations.source_reference: Directly supported by the uploaded Unit 3 Part A handout.

detailed_explanations.detailed_explanation: Amylose is reported to give a blue iodine colour; amylopectin is described as purple in the source. The handout cautions that a fixed 660 nm specification is not verified in the accessible text.
detailed_explanations.source_reference: Directly supported by the uploaded Unit 3 Part A handout.

detailed_explanations.correct_answer: Containing starch with very low amylose
detailed_explanations.detailed_explanation: The source flags the phrase 'zero starch' as an error. Waxy maize is starch-rich but has very low amylose and a high amylopectin proportion.
detailed_explanations.source_reference: Directly supported by the uploaded Unit 3 Part A handout.

detailed_explanations.detailed_explanation: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Gelatinization is a supramolecular transition involving hydration, swelling and loss of native order. It does not mean that all glycosidic bonds have been hydrolysed.
detailed_explanations.source_reference: Directly supported by the uploaded Unit 3 Part A handout.

detailed_explanations.correct_answer: Disruption of the organized native granule structure
detailed_explanations.detailed_explanation: Birefringence reflects ordered granule organization. Its disappearance is associated with gelatinization and loss of native structural order.
detailed_explanations.source_reference: Directly supported by the uploaded Unit 3 Part A handout.

detailed_explanations.correct_answer: Gelatinization onset and swelling vary with botanical source and conditions
detailed_explanations.detailed_explanation: The handout reconciles different ranges: some starches begin swelling near 55°C, others near 85°C, and observed thickening or extensive swelling can occur at different temperatures. Onset and endpoint are not identical.
detailed_explanations.source_reference: Directly supported by the uploaded Unit 3 Part A handout.

detailed_explanations.detailed_explanation: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Amylose reassociates relatively rapidly, while amylopectin reorganizes more slowly during storage. Both fractions can participate, and staling also involves moisture redistribution, crumb firming and aroma changes.
detailed_explanations.source_reference: Directly supported by the uploaded Unit 3 Part A handout.

detailed_explanations.correct_answer: A combination of starch reorganization, moisture redistribution and other quality changes
detailed_explanations.detailed_explanation: The handout explicitly warns against reducing staling to evaporation alone. Retrogradation, crumb firming, reduced elasticity, moisture redistribution and aroma changes contribute.
detailed_explanations.source_reference: Directly supported by the uploaded Unit 3 Part A handout.

detailed_explanations.correct_answer: Can develop viscosity or hydrate in cold water without the normal cooking step
detailed_explanations.detailed_explanation: Pregelatinization disrupts native granule order before use, enabling cold-water hydration and thickening. It is a functional modification, not a guarantee of universal stability.
detailed_explanations.source_reference: Directly supported by the uploaded Unit 3 Part A handout.

detailed_explanations.detailed_explanation: Cross-links reinforce the starch structure and can improve tolerance to heat, shear and acidic processing. Exact performance depends on the reagent and degree of modification.
detailed_explanations.source_reference: Directly supported by the uploaded Unit 3 Part A handout.

detailed_explanations.detailed_explanation: All three statements match the handout. Degree of esterification describes the esterified carboxyl fraction. High-methoxyl pectin requires acidic, high-soluble-solids conditions, whereas low-methoxyl pectin commonly forms calcium-mediated networks.
detailed_explanations.source_reference: Directly supported by the uploaded Unit 3 Part A handout.

detailed_explanations.correct_answer: The proportion of galacturonic acid carboxyl groups present as methyl esters
detailed_explanations.detailed_explanation: DE describes the proportion of galacturonic acid carboxyl groups esterified, commonly as methyl esters. It influences the conditions and mechanism of pectin gel formation.
detailed_explanations.source_reference: Directly supported by the uploaded Unit 3 Part A handout.

detailed_explanations.detailed_explanation: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Alginate's principal residues are mannuronic and guluronic acids; guar and locust bean gums contain mannose backbones with galactose substitution. Inulin is a fructan, not a glucan.
detailed_explanations.source_reference: Directly supported by the uploaded Unit 3 Part A handout.

detailed_explanations.detailed_explanation: Calcium ions can bridge suitable carboxylate groups on low-methoxyl pectin chains. The handout flags exact universal pH/solids intervals and a detailed egg-box model as not fully verified in the accessible pages.
detailed_explanations.source_reference: Directly supported by the uploaded Unit 3 Part A handout.

detailed_explanations.detailed_explanation: Agar is a seaweed hydrocolloid associated with red algae. It forms thermoreversible gels and is used as a gelling agent.
detailed_explanations.source_reference: Directly supported by the uploaded Unit 3 Part A handout.

detailed_explanations.detailed_explanation: The detailed source passage correctly identifies alginate's monomers as mannuronic and guluronic acids. The handout flags an inconsistent table elsewhere and instructs readers not to follow the erroneous monomer identification.
detailed_explanations.source_reference: Directly supported by the uploaded Unit 3 Part A handout.

detailed_explanations.detailed_explanation: The source describes galactomannans with mannose backbones and galactose side groups. A line giving a mannose-to-glucose ratio is flagged as an apparent error.
detailed_explanations.source_reference: Directly supported by the uploaded Unit 3 Part A handout.

detailed_explanations.correct_answer: Recognition of particular glycosidic linkages and substrate structure
detailed_explanations.detailed_explanation: Polysaccharide-degrading enzymes recognize particular linkage types and structural contexts. Therefore, polymers made from the same monomer can have very different digestibility and functionality.
detailed_explanations.source_reference: Directly supported by the uploaded Unit 3 Part A handout.

detailed_explanations.detailed_explanation: At pI, positive and negative charges balance so the net charge is approximately zero. Individual ionizable groups may still carry charges; pI does not mean absence of local charge.
detailed_explanations.source_reference: Directly supported by the uploaded Unit 3 Part A handout.

detailed_explanations.detailed_explanation: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. At pI, positive and negative charges balance on average, but individual groups may remain charged. Reduced electrostatic repulsion can contribute to lower solubility or precipitation.
detailed_explanations.source_reference: Directly supported by the uploaded Unit 3 Part A handout.

detailed_explanations.correct_answer: Salt increasing electrostatic screening and protein solubility
detailed_explanations.detailed_explanation: At lower ionic strength, salts can screen attractive electrostatic interactions and improve solubility. At higher salt concentrations, competition for water and other effects can promote salting-out.
detailed_explanations.source_reference: Directly supported by the uploaded Unit 3 Part A handout.

detailed_explanations.detailed_explanation: The source identifies albumins as water-soluble, globulins as soluble in suitable dilute salt solutions, prolamins as alcohol-soluble and glutelins as soluble under suitable dilute acid or base conditions.
detailed_explanations.source_reference: Directly supported by the uploaded Unit 3 Part A handout.

detailed_explanations.detailed_explanation: Casein is a phosphoprotein. Some fractions may also have carbohydrate substitution, but the handout cautions against labelling every casein molecule identically as a glycoprotein.
detailed_explanations.source_reference: Directly supported by the uploaded Unit 3 Part A handout.

detailed_explanations.detailed_explanation: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Denaturation changes conformation and accessibility without necessarily changing primary structure. Peptide-bond cleavage is hydrolysis, a distinct chemical event.
detailed_explanations.source_reference: Directly supported by the uploaded Unit 3 Part A handout.

detailed_explanations.detailed_explanation: Heat is a major denaturing treatment; pH, salts, solvents, pressure and interfaces can also alter protein conformation. The source's 60–90°C example is not a universal inactivation schedule.
detailed_explanations.source_reference: Directly supported by the uploaded Unit 3 Part A handout.

detailed_explanations.correct_answer: Denaturation alters conformation, whereas hydrolysis cleaves peptide bonds
detailed_explanations.detailed_explanation: Denaturation changes protein folding/association; hydrolysis chemically cleaves peptide bonds and can reduce chain length. They may occur together during processing but are not synonyms.
detailed_explanations.source_reference: Directly supported by the uploaded Unit 3 Part A handout.

detailed_explanations.correct_answer: Removal or conversion of an amide group
detailed_explanations.detailed_explanation: Deamidation changes side-chain amide functionality, for example in asparagine or glutamine residues. It can alter charge and protein functionality.
detailed_explanations.source_reference: Directly supported by the uploaded Unit 3 Part A handout.

detailed_explanations.correct_answer: Conversion between D- and L-configurations at a chiral centre
detailed_explanations.detailed_explanation: Racemization changes stereochemistry, producing the opposite enantiomeric configuration at a chiral amino-acid centre. Severe alkaline or thermal processing can promote it.
detailed_explanations.source_reference: Directly supported by the uploaded Unit 3 Part A handout.

detailed_explanations.correct_answer: It can modify amino-acid side chains and affect functionality
detailed_explanations.detailed_explanation: Oxidation can modify susceptible residues and promote aggregation or cross-linking, changing solubility, texture and nutritional quality. The effect depends on the protein and processing environment.
detailed_explanations.source_reference: Directly supported by the uploaded Unit 3 Part A handout.

detailed_explanations.detailed_explanation: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Dehydroalanine is a reactive intermediate and lysine addition can form lysinoalanine. Severe alkaline processing can instead reduce nutritional availability and promote racemization or other modifications.
detailed_explanations.source_reference: Directly supported by the uploaded Unit 3 Part A handout.

detailed_explanations.detailed_explanation: The ε-amino group of lysine can add to dehydroalanine, forming lysinoalanine cross-links. The reaction can reduce nutritional availability and alter proteolytic cleavage.
detailed_explanations.source_reference: Directly supported by the uploaded Unit 3 Part A handout.

detailed_explanations.detailed_explanation: Cysteine addition to dehydroalanine forms lanthionine; lysine forms lysinoalanine and ornithine can form ornithoalanine. These are distinct alkaline-processing cross-links.
detailed_explanations.source_reference: Directly supported by the uploaded Unit 3 Part A handout.

detailed_explanations.correct_answer: Formation of modified amino acids and reduced availability of essential residues
detailed_explanations.detailed_explanation: Severe alkaline exposure can cause dehydroalanine-mediated cross-links, racemization and other modifications. These can reduce digestibility or amino-acid availability.
detailed_explanations.source_reference: Directly supported by the uploaded Unit 3 Part A handout.

detailed_explanations.correct_answer: A concentrated protein solution prepared for extrusion through a spinneret
detailed_explanations.detailed_explanation: The handout describes purified protein isolate and a dope generally around 10–40% protein, solubilized under alkaline conditions and extruded through a spinneret into a coagulation bath.
detailed_explanations.source_reference: Directly supported by the uploaded Unit 3 Part A handout.

detailed_explanations.detailed_explanation: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Gliadin and glutenin are protein fractions with complementary viscoelastic functions. They are not carbohydrate polymers.
detailed_explanations.source_reference: Directly supported by the uploaded Unit 3 Part A handout.

detailed_explanations.detailed_explanation: The source describes alkaline solubilization near pH 10. Prolonged alkaline residence is a concern because it can promote protein damage and undesirable cross-links.
detailed_explanations.source_reference: Directly supported by the uploaded Unit 3 Part A handout.

detailed_explanations.correct_answer: Uses heat, moisture, pressure and shear to restructure protein in a barrel and die
detailed_explanations.detailed_explanation: The handout describes high-protein feed, roughly 30–40% moisture, elevated temperature and pressure, directional restructuring and die pressure release. It produces a textured matrix rather than the same spun-fibre structure.
detailed_explanations.source_reference: Directly supported by the uploaded Unit 3 Part A handout.

detailed_explanations.detailed_explanation: The handout gives approximately 150–200°C, 10–20 MPa and 30–40% moisture for its described extrusion process. These are process-specific examples, not universal specifications for every extruder.
detailed_explanations.source_reference: Directly supported by the uploaded Unit 3 Part A handout.

detailed_explanations.detailed_explanation: Gliadin contributes viscosity and extensibility, while glutenin contributes elasticity and strength. Their hydrated network gives dough its characteristic viscoelastic behaviour.
detailed_explanations.source_reference: Directly supported by the uploaded Unit 3 Part A handout.

detailed_explanations.detailed_explanation: Glutenin contributes elastic strength and recovery, whereas gliadin contributes viscous flow and extensibility. Dough performance depends on the balance between the two.
detailed_explanations.source_reference: Directly supported by the uploaded Unit 3 Part A handout.

detailed_explanations.detailed_explanation: Chymosin cleaves κ-casein, destabilizing the casein micelle surface layer. Aggregation of destabilized micelles follows as a second stage.
detailed_explanations.source_reference: Directly supported by the uploaded Unit 3 Part A handout.

detailed_explanations.detailed_explanation: Chymosin first cleaves κ-casein, weakening steric/electrostatic stabilization of micelles. The destabilized micelles then aggregate, especially under suitable calcium and temperature conditions.
detailed_explanations.source_reference: Directly supported by the uploaded Unit 3 Part A handout.

detailed_explanations.detailed_explanation: Avidin binds biotin with very high affinity, making biotin less available. The handout includes avidin as a key egg-white protein/function example.
detailed_explanations.source_reference: Directly supported by the uploaded Unit 3 Part A handout.

detailed_explanations.detailed_explanation: Maillard browning and caramelization are non-enzymatic; polyphenol-oxidase browning is enzyme-initiated. Similar brown colour can arise through different substrates and mechanisms.
detailed_explanations.source_reference: Directly supported by the uploaded Unit 3 Part A handout.

detailed_explanations.correct_answer: A reducing carbonyl compound and an available amino group
detailed_explanations.detailed_explanation: Maillard chemistry begins with carbonyl–amine condensation, commonly involving a reducing sugar and amino groups in amino acids or proteins. It does not require a proteinaceous enzyme.
detailed_explanations.source_reference: Directly supported by the uploaded Unit 3 Part A handout.

detailed_explanations.detailed_explanation: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Maillard browning is a non-enzymatic carbonyl–amine reaction. Oxygen is not obligatory for the initial condensation, unlike PPO browning.
detailed_explanations.source_reference: Directly supported by the uploaded Unit 3 Part A handout.

detailed_explanations.detailed_explanation: Aldose-derived Maillard intermediates undergo Amadori rearrangement to more stable deoxy-ketosyl products. The handout flags the detailed ketose-specific Heyns pathway as not fully developed in the accessible source pages.
detailed_explanations.source_reference: Directly supported by the uploaded Unit 3 Part A handout.

detailed_explanations.correct_answer: Oxygen is not obligatory for the initial carbonyl–amine condensation
detailed_explanations.detailed_explanation: The initial Maillard condensation does not require oxygen as an obligatory reactant. Oxygen is essential to the polyphenol-oxidase browning system.
detailed_explanations.source_reference: Directly supported by the uploaded Unit 3 Part A handout.

detailed_explanations.correct_answer: Reducing pentoses > reducing hexoses > reducing disaccharides
detailed_explanations.detailed_explanation: The handout gives reducing pentoses > reducing hexoses > reducing disaccharides as a useful general trend, while explicitly qualifying it as non-universal and dependent on conditions and reactant identity.
detailed_explanations.source_reference: Directly supported by the uploaded Unit 3 Part A handout.

detailed_explanations.detailed_explanation: The unprotonated amino form R–NH2 is generally the more effective nucleophile. Increasing pH often raises its fraction, although reaction pathways and matrix conditions also matter.
detailed_explanations.source_reference: Directly supported by the uploaded Unit 3 Part A handout.

detailed_explanations.detailed_explanation: All three statements are supported. The schematic describes limited mobility at very low aw, increased mobility at intermediate aw and dilution at high aw. The numerical optimum is a qualified teaching relationship, not a universal constant.
detailed_explanations.source_reference: Directly supported by the uploaded Unit 3 Part A handout.

detailed_explanations.correct_answer: One fewer carbon than the amino acid
detailed_explanations.detailed_explanation: The carboxyl carbon is released as carbon dioxide, leaving a Strecker aldehyde with one fewer carbon atom. These aldehydes contribute characteristic food aromas.
detailed_explanations.source_reference: Directly supported by the uploaded Unit 3 Part A handout.

detailed_explanations.detailed_explanation: Free asparagine is the principal amino-acid precursor in the recognized sugar–asparagine route to acrylamide. Lysine blockage is a separate nutritional consequence of Maillard chemistry.
detailed_explanations.source_reference: Directly supported by the uploaded Unit 3 Part A handout.

detailed_explanations.detailed_explanation: Reactive carbonyls can modify lysine's ε-amino group and reduce available lysine before conspicuous brown pigment appears. Colour intensity is therefore not a reliable direct measure of nutritional damage.
detailed_explanations.source_reference: Directly supported by the uploaded Unit 3 Part A handout.

detailed_explanations.correct_answer: Strecker aldehydes are volatile flavour compounds; melanoidins are later brown condensed products
detailed_explanations.detailed_explanation: Strecker degradation yields volatile aldehydes associated with aroma. Melanoidins are brown products formed through later condensation of Maillard intermediates.
detailed_explanations.source_reference: Directly supported by the uploaded Unit 3 Part A handout.

detailed_explanations.correct_answer: The rate constants of chemical steps generally increase with temperature
detailed_explanations.detailed_explanation: Higher temperature generally accelerates condensation, rearrangement and degradation steps. The overall reaction is a network, so different products can have different apparent kinetics.
detailed_explanations.source_reference: Directly supported by the uploaded Unit 3 Part A handout.

detailed_explanations.correct_answer: Is sugar degradation without a required amino reactant
detailed_explanations.detailed_explanation: Caramelization involves sugar rearrangement, dehydration, fragmentation and condensation without requiring an amino reactant. Maillard browning begins with carbonyl–amine chemistry.
detailed_explanations.source_reference: Directly supported by the uploaded Unit 3 Part A handout.

detailed_explanations.detailed_explanation: The handout describes structural rearrangement and enolization, dehydration, fragmentation, and condensation into coloured material. Volatile compounds contribute aroma while condensed products contribute colour.
detailed_explanations.source_reference: Directly supported by the uploaded Unit 3 Part A handout.

detailed_explanations.detailed_explanation: Only statement 2 is correct. Caramelization is sugar degradation without a required amino reactant. The handout describes rearrangement/enolization, dehydration, fragmentation and condensation; temperature depends on sugar identity and processing conditions.
detailed_explanations.source_reference: Directly supported by the uploaded Unit 3 Part A handout.

detailed_explanations.detailed_explanation: The handout lists caramelans as C12H18O9, caramelens as C36H50O25 and caramelins as C125H188O80. These are traditional empirical designations, not proof of unique pure compounds.
detailed_explanations.source_reference: Directly supported by the uploaded Unit 3 Part A handout.

detailed_explanations.correct_answer: Active enzyme, suitable phenolic substrate and oxygen
detailed_explanations.detailed_explanation: Tissue disruption brings active polyphenol oxidase, phenolic substrates and oxygen into contact. Quinones form and then undergo largely non-enzymatic reactions that generate brown pigments.
detailed_explanations.source_reference: Directly supported by the uploaded Unit 3 Part A handout.

detailed_explanations.detailed_explanation: Polyphenol oxidase is a copper-containing oxidoreductase. Copper is involved in its catalytic centre and oxygen participates in the oxidation reaction.
detailed_explanations.source_reference: Directly supported by the uploaded Unit 3 Part A handout.

detailed_explanations.correct_answer: Hydroxylation of a suitable monophenol to an ortho-diphenol
detailed_explanations.detailed_explanation: Cresolase activity hydroxylates a suitable monophenol to an ortho-diphenol. Catecholase activity then oxidizes an ortho-diphenol to an ortho-quinone.
detailed_explanations.source_reference: Directly supported by the uploaded Unit 3 Part A handout.

detailed_explanations.correct_answer: Oxidation of an ortho-diphenol to an ortho-quinone
detailed_explanations.detailed_explanation: Catecholase/diphenolase activity oxidizes ortho-diphenols to ortho-quinones. Quinones are reactive intermediates that can couple and condense into pigment-forming products.
detailed_explanations.source_reference: Directly supported by the uploaded Unit 3 Part A handout.

detailed_explanations.detailed_explanation: Polyphenol oxidase generates reactive ortho-quinones. These undergo addition, coupling and condensation reactions, many of which are non-enzymatic, producing melanin-like pigments.
detailed_explanations.source_reference: Directly supported by the uploaded Unit 3 Part A handout.

detailed_explanations.detailed_explanation: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. PPO contains a copper catalytic centre and catalyses phenolic oxidation to quinones. Molecular oxygen is a required reactant in this oxidative browning system.
detailed_explanations.source_reference: Directly supported by the uploaded Unit 3 Part A handout.

detailed_explanations.detailed_explanation: A validated thermal blanching treatment denatures/inactivates the enzyme. It must be sufficient throughout the product, but excessive heating can soften tissue and cause nutrient losses.
detailed_explanations.source_reference: Directly supported by the uploaded Unit 3 Part A handout.

detailed_explanations.correct_answer: Restricting an essential reactant for phenolic oxidation
detailed_explanations.detailed_explanation: Molecular oxygen is required for the oxidative enzyme reaction. Deaeration, barrier packaging or immersion can reduce oxygen access, but leakage or later exposure can allow browning to resume.
detailed_explanations.source_reference: Directly supported by the uploaded Unit 3 Part A handout.

detailed_explanations.detailed_explanation: Citric acid lowers pH and can complex metals, both of which may suppress productive enzyme activity. The handout cautions that a low-pH target is not a universal irreversible inactivation rule.
detailed_explanations.source_reference: Directly supported by the uploaded Unit 3 Part A handout.

detailed_explanations.correct_answer: Intercepting quinones and forming sulfonated products
detailed_explanations.detailed_explanation: Reactive sulfur species can intercept quinones and form sulfonated products, reducing pigment formation. Their use must comply with applicable legal limits, labelling and consumer-sensitivity requirements.
detailed_explanations.source_reference: Directly supported by the uploaded Unit 3 Part A handout.

detailed_explanations.correct_answer: Maillard begins with carbonyl–amine chemistry, while PPO browning begins with enzyme-catalysed phenol oxidation
detailed_explanations.detailed_explanation: Maillard initiation is carbonyl–amine condensation and does not require an enzyme or obligatory oxygen. PPO browning requires active copper-containing enzyme, phenolic substrate and oxygen.
detailed_explanations.source_reference: Directly supported by the uploaded Unit 3 Part A handout.

detailed_explanations.detailed_explanation: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Ascorbic acid gives reserve-dependent quinone reduction, while blanching targets enzyme activity. Sulfite application is subject to applicable legal permissions, residual limits, labelling and consumer-sensitivity considerations.
detailed_explanations.source_reference: Directly supported by the uploaded Unit 3 Part A handout.

detailed_explanations.correct_answer: Combine mechanism-based controls and validate residual enzyme activity, colour stability and product safety
detailed_explanations.detailed_explanation: The handout recommends combined, product-specific controls and validation. Relevant checks include residual enzyme activity, storage colour, antioxidant depletion where relevant, sensory quality and microbiological safety.
detailed_explanations.source_reference: Directly supported by the uploaded Unit 3 Part A handout.

quality_control.note: Structural and consistency checks passed. Scientific content has been checked against the uploaded handout and its stated qualifications; this is not an official HPSC paper or a guarantee of future questions.
